shouldFix.title: The Linux namespace identity is not race-bound to the mountinfo observation
evidence: The contract requires the {pid,starttime} pair immediately before and after reading mountinfo. That detects PID reuse, but setns(2) or unshare(2) can change the same live process's mount namespace without changing either member of the pair.

mountNamespaceIdentity is described as an inode bound to observerProcessIdentity and later events must equal it, but the contract never requires the namespace inode to be observed and equal immediately before and after the mountinfo read, nor does it hold a namespace handle across that read.
Therefore mountinfo may describe one namespace while the retained baseline inode describes another, even though every specified {pid,starttime} check passes.
shouldFix.impact: A qualification run can freeze a mount-record/type observation and a namespace baseline that were never simultaneously true. Later equality checks can then validate against the wrong namespace and cannot prove the preselection volume decision.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Read and require the same /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt identity immediately before and after the mountinfo observation, bound to the same before/after {pid,starttime} pair, or hold an open namespace handle that supplies an equivalent atomic binding. Refuse on any mismatch and retain that bound observation.

shouldFix.title: The new preselection and later volume evidence is still not a closed retained-data schema
evidence: retainedEventSchema is a flat list of per-event field labels, yet it adds fields marked 'qualification-run only' without defining a run record, preselection event kind, required placement, cardinality, or conditional presence rules.

PreselectionFilesystemObservation appears only in evidenceJoin and is not defined as an object anywhere. The join then says the three-member observation must equal two later scalar fields instead of defining equality for canonicalVerifiedRoot, volumeIdentity, and filesystemTypeToken separately.

linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity is required to 'prove retargeting' but has no value shape, observation source, serialization, or equality rule. The OS-tagged f_fsid and {decodedMountPoint,device} values likewise have no closed serialized forms.
shouldFix.impact: Mutually incompatible producers can all claim the retained schema, and a verifier cannot determine whether exactly one preselection baseline existed or whether each later event matched its volume/type and Linux record. The repair adds names but not independently checkable retained evidence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define a closed qualification-run record or explicit preselection event kind with exactly one canonical root, OS-tagged volume identity, filesystem token, observer identity, namespace conditional, and Linux selected-record identity. Define closed later-event forms and exact per-field equality/refusal joins, including serialization and OS-specific required/absent rules.

shouldFix.title: The verifiedInstallRoot serialization silently drops the predecessor's Unicode normalization rule
evidence: V10 serialized verifiedInstallRoot as an NFC Unicode path. V11 replaces that scalar with treeRootToken, otherTokens, join, and equality fields, but none names a character encoding or Unicode normalization rule for non-root tokens.

File 04 Exact-byte delivery requires explicit Unicode rules. POSIX separators plus rejection of empty, dot, and dot-dot components does not decide whether normalization occurs, which form is canonical, or when byte equality is computed.
The change is on the declared succession roster, but honestyRepairsFromV10 does not disclose the removal as an intentional semantic change.
shouldFix.impact: Implementations can sign or compare canonically equivalent path spellings differently, and macOS and Linux producers can diverge on the exact bytes fed to join and canonicalization. The supposedly exact signed preselection binding is not reproducible across conforming implementations.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restore an explicit encoding and normalization rule, including ordering before grammar validation and signing, or state an equally exact byte policy with rejection behavior. If NFC remains intended, carry it into otherTokens and define UTF-8 serialization and byte equality after NFC.
